title: Sequential Integer Square Root
constraints: `root = ⌊√x⌋` for a 16-bit unsigned `x`, computed one result bit per cycle.

An edge with `start` while idle captures `x` and sets `busy`. The result is ready exactly **8** edges later: after that edge `busy = 0`, `done = 1` (for one cycle), and `root` holds the result until the next start. `start` while busy is ignored.
No `/` or `%`. A multiplier is allowed. Synchronous reset → idle, `done = 0`, `root = 0`.
hints: Decide one bit per cycle, from bit 7 down to 0: `cand = root | (1 << i)`, and keep it if `cand * cand <= x`.
The non-restoring version avoids the multiplier: keep a remainder and subtract `(root << 2 | 1) << …`. Try it once the simple version passes.
`root` must be cleared at start (it is built up bit by bit).
